intro: You're looking for a clinic that can carry out a frozen embryo transfer, probably because you already have embryos in storage and are thinking about the next step. Finding a clinic near you matters for the monitoring and appointments that come with a transfer cycle. We can introduce you to a UK fertility clinic that offers frozen embryo transfer, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a frozen embryo transfer near me usually need
need_lead: A local clinic that can plan and carry out a frozen embryo transfer, with appointments you can realistically get to.
needs: You have embryos in storage from a previous cycle and want to use one in a transfer, so you need a clinic that can thaw and transfer them.
You are moving home or changing clinics and need a local provider to take over the transfer part of your treatment.
You want a clinic within easy travelling distance because a frozen embryo transfer involves scans and monitoring appointments in the run-up.
You are considering a natural or medicated cycle for your transfer and want to discuss which approach suits you with a local professional.
You have been advised that a frozen embryo transfer is an option and want to find a nearby licensed clinic to talk it through.
context_heading: Understanding licensing for frozen embryo transfer
context: Treatment involving eggs, sperm or embryos, including a frozen embryo transfer, should always be carried out at a clinic licensed by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA). The HFEA's Choose a Fertility Clinic tool lets you see each licensed clinic's inspection ratings, success rates and patient feedback, which can help you compare local options.

A frozen embryo transfer thaws a stored embryo and places it in the womb, either in a natural cycle timed around your own ovulation or in a medicated cycle. It usually involves less medication than a fresh IVF cycle, and the timing is planned around your cycle. Ask the clinic how they plan transfers and what monitoring is involved.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you are looking for a frozen embryo transfer near you, and give your location or the area you can travel to.
Explain whether you already have embryos in storage and, if so, where they are stored.
Say whether you have had a frozen embryo transfer before or whether this would be your first.
Let us know if you have a preference for a natural or medicated cycle, or if you are unsure and would like to discuss it.
Include any relevant medical history that the clinic might need to know about, such as previous fertility treatment.
Tell us your preferred way to be contacted and any times you are available for an initial conversation.
questions: Are you licensed by the HFEA to carry out frozen embryo transfers?

faqs.q: Do I need a referral from my GP to have a frozen embryo transfer at a clinic?
faqs.a: Many fertility clinics accept self-referrals for frozen embryo transfers, but some may ask for information from your GP or the clinic that stored your embryos. It is worth asking the clinic what they need before you book.

faqs.q: Can I have a frozen embryo transfer at a clinic that is not near my home?
faqs.a: You can choose any licensed clinic, but a frozen embryo transfer involves several monitoring appointments, so travelling distance can matter in practice. A clinic nearer to you may make the cycle easier to manage alongside work and daily life.

faqs.q: How long does a frozen embryo transfer cycle take?
faqs.a: The length of a frozen embryo transfer cycle varies depending on whether it is a natural or medicated cycle and on your own cycle. The clinic will explain the likely timeline for you at your consultation.

faqs.q: Will I need to take medication for a frozen embryo transfer?
faqs.a: A medicated cycle uses medication to prepare the womb lining, while a natural cycle relies on your own hormones and usually involves less medication. The clinic can discuss which approach is suitable for your circumstances.
